[1/6] Plan: prove and fix four HTTP/file defects - huge numeric ids and offsets must answer 400 not 500; chunked JSON must be read across chunk boundaries; a new photo must never overwrite a rival file placed at the same name; JSON replies must never be browser-cached

impact_assessment.why: A code audit of the request, store and catalog paths found four reproducible robustness/privacy gaps that survive 188 passing tests: SQLite rejects Python ints over 2^63-1 with an uncaught OverflowError after album/trash/offset parsing, Request.json reads only one chunk of a chunked body, ingest moves a temp file over an existing name before the catalog rejects the clash, and per-person JSON replies carry no Cache-Control so a browser may reuse one profile's data after a sign-in switch
impact_assessment.benefits: Malformed input answers a clear 400 instead of a 500 traceback; chunked JSON clients work; two processes adding a same-named photo cannot destroy the first file; private API data is never cached on disk
impact_assessment.risks: contract: HTTP errors and store placement order change, existing clients keep working; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: new exclusive-create path closes a server-vs-CLI race without changing the in-process lock; state: no schema or format change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add failing-first unit and HTTP tests, keep every message inside the Error/Why/Fix shape, change only the three bounded modules plus messages, atomic_file and store, run the full 188-test suite and 4/4 project gates before committing, and record the decisions in ADR-031

[1/4] Plan: drop cached previews whose photo is gone at Harbor start, with a failing-first prune test, README and ADR-032

impact_assessment.why: The preview cache under .harbor/thumbs keeps a JPEG for every photo ever previewed. Deleting a photo forever, emptying trash, or removing it in File Explorer leaves that JPEG behind, so a long-lived library slowly accumulates dead cache files that the Storage tab cannot explain
impact_assessment.benefits: Reclaims orphaned preview bytes on every start, keeps the cache bounded by the live catalog, and is safe because previews are disposable and regenerated on demand
impact_assessment.risks: contract: only cache files outside the live SHA-256 set are touched; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: startup runs before server threads start; state: cache-only deletion, no catalog or photo change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Implement prune on Thumbnailer over the two-level SHA cache, pass the catalog's live hashes from HarborApp, ignore a locked preview without aborting, test orphan removal and live retention, and run all 202+ tests plus 4/4 gates before committing

[1/4] Plan: make startup temp cleanup age-based so a running Harbor's fresh upload buffer or prepared ZIP is never deleted by a CLI import/second instance; failing-first tests, README/ADR-033

impact_assessment.why: PhotoStore.__init__ unlinks every .tmp_upload_* in .harbor/incoming and Downloads.clean unlinks every .zip in .harbor/downloads. A CLI import constructs a second HarborApp against the same library while the server is running, so its startup cleanup can delete the server's in-progress upload or a prepared download that has a live token
impact_assessment.benefits: Starting a CLI command or a second Harbor window no longer breaks an upload or download already in flight; only abandoned buffers older than the cleanup threshold are removed
impact_assessment.risks: contract: cleanup timing changes, not the paths or API; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: age check narrows the cross-process window without pretending to lock across processes; state: stale files may live up to the threshold instead of being deleted immediately
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use a six-hour age gate for uploads and a one-hour gate for downloads (their tokens expire in 15 minutes), test fresh versus stale buffers, keep unlink failures non-fatal, run the full suite and 4/4 gates, and record ADR-033
